Critics also question sanctions’ effectiveness and warn against Europe’s growing dependence on the United States.

Zelensky: Replacing Me Won’t Change Ukraine’s Need for Defense — Responding to Trump’s call for a new Ukrainian leader, Zelensky said replacing him would not remove Ukraine’s determination to resist Russia. He ruled out resigning and said constant Russian attacks make elections nearly impossible.

UK Pledges $23M for Chornobyl Repairs Amid Support Strains — The UK pledged £17 million ($23 million) toward repairs to the New Safe Confinement at Chornobyl, damaged by a Russian drone strike in February 2025. The contribution is part of a wider international effort, with total repair costs estimated above €500 million. The pledge comes as far-right parties challenge continued aid to Kyiv and Ukraine faces disruption to military satellite communications.

Moscow Arrests Swede Accused of Planning Attacks — Russia’s FSB said it had arrested a Swedish national in the Pskov region, accusing him of fighting for Ukraine, illegally crossing the Russian border and planning sabotage attacks on military facilities. The agency said a criminal case had been opened on charges including terrorism and mercenary activity.

US Threatened Immediate Intelligence Cutoff Unless Ukraine Halts Strikes — US intelligence officials warned Ukraine that further strikes on Russian energy infrastructure could trigger an immediate intelligence cutoff.

Musk Tells Zelensky to ‘Go’ as Ukraine Questions US Support — Elon Musk told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Kyiv accused Washington of undermining its defenses through Starlink restrictions and gaps in intelligence sharing. The dispute comes amid Russian missile attacks, concerns over US support and tensions over Washington’s diesel deal with Moscow.

Romania Says Eight People Missing After Fire on Vessel in Black Sea — A fire aboard the San Marino-flagged vessel Wine Trader off Romania’s Black Sea coast left eight people missing and four rescued on Oct. 15. Authorities launched a search operation but have not confirmed a drone strike. The incident follows another suspected drone attack on a tanker off Romania on Wednesday.

Trump – The Gift That Keeps Giving to Putin — Tim Ash argues that Trump misunderstands Putin’s imperial ambitions and risks undermining NATO by pressuring Ukraine into territorial concessions. He believes Putin will exploit Western divisions to pursue further gains, while Ukraine and Europe must prepare for a prolonged war and greater European defense independence.

‘We’re Done’: Zelensky Says Ukraine Will Resume Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries — Zelensky said Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries despite US pressure to halt attacks, accusing Trump of favoring Moscow. He warned that US restrictions on intelligence sharing and Starlink could cost Ukrainian lives as Russia intensifies missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure.

Trump Weighs Easing Shadow Fleet Sanctions to Lower Oil Shipping Costs — The Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on shadow fleet tankers to lower oil shipping costs amid disruptions to global energy supplies. The move follows Trump’s decision to lift restrictions on Russian diesel, which drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who warned it would help finance Russia’s war against Ukraine.

‘Putin Is Laughing’ – Zelensky Calls Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal a Victory for Moscow — In an interview with Piers Morgan, Zelensky described Trump’s Russian diesel deal as a tactical victory for Putin, warning that Moscow was exploiting Washington’s decisions to pressure Ukraine into concessions. He criticized Starlink restrictions and cited heavy Russian battlefield losses, while Morgan urged Trump to stop appeasing Putin, comparing the Russian leader to Hitler.

Russia Exploits Starlink Disruptions to Launch Massive Drone Barrage on Ukraine – Zelensky — Russia launched at least 269 drones against Ukraine overnight and throughout Wednesday, killing six people and injuring 13 in Lutsk. Zelensky warned that Moscow was exploiting Starlink disruptions affecting Ukrainian interceptor drones and urged stronger sanctions and military support. Britain pledged to accelerate deliveries of air defense weapons.

King Charles Welcomes Zelensky as Britain Steps Up Military Support for Ukraine — King Charles III hosted Zelensky at Buckingham Palace before the Ukrainian president met Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who pledged faster air defense missile deliveries and tougher sanctions against Russia. The visit underscored Britain’s continued support for Ukraine as Russian attacks intensify and Kyiv faces uncertainty over US military assistance.

Zelensky Says Starlink Was Switched Off During Russian Attacks – ‘People Are Dying Because of This Decision’ — Zelensky said Starlink restrictions during Russian attacks were deliberate, warning that disrupted communications weakened Ukraine’s air defenses and cost civilian lives. US lawmakers from both parties condemned the restrictions, while SpaceX pointed to US government control of military-grade Starshield.

Russian Drones Pound Kropyvnytskyi, Killing Three and Injuring Six — Three people were killed and six injured in a massive Russian drone attack on Kropyvnytskyi. Residential buildings, vehicles, transport facilities and industrial sites were damaged.

General Staff Reports 222 Clashes on Wednesday as Russia Continues Pressing Pokrovsk Axis — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) recorded 222 battles with Russian forces throughout Wednesday, Oct. 14, with the heaviest assaults on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes. Russia used more than 5,000 kamikaze drones and at least 190 guided aerial bombs (KABs).

Musk Says US Government Controls Ukraine’s Starshield Limits as Zelensky Accuses Russia of Exploiting Outage — SpaceX’s Elon Musk said limits on Ukraine’s military Starshield service are set by the US military and ultimately US President Donald Trump, as President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of exploiting the outage to escalate its drone attacks. Meanwhile, the UK agreed to speed up air defense deliveries after Zelensky met British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday, Oct. 14

Saving Lives on the Front Line: Kyiv Post’s Jason Smart Hits €1M Milestone — Organized alongside security analyst Sergej Sumlenny, the campaign drew 8,585 global contributors to supply frontline combat units with tailored drones, and critical medical gear to help Ukraine’s Army defeat Russia.

EU Disburses Another €2.86B to Cover Ukraine’s ‘Most Urgent Needs’ – Drones and Missiles — The European Union (EU) has disbursed another €2.86 billion ($3.1 billion) to Ukraine under the defense component of its €90 billion (approx. $100 billion) Ukraine Support Loan, according to Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi and the European Commission on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The funds are allocated for air defense, particularly drones and missiles, ahead of the country’s fifth year of Russia’s aggression.

Zelensky Says He Feels Betrayed By the US, Warns Ukraine Is Losing America as Partner — Speaking during an interview on “Piers Morgan Uncensored,” released on Wednesday, Oct. 14, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine is losing America as a strong partner, blaming US President Donald Trump’s advisers for pushing him to the “wrong side.” He also called Elon Musk’s Starlink restrictions “a big mistake,” warning that Ukrainian citizens will continue dying, as Russia increases its terror on Ukrai

Russian Strikes Destroy Epicentr K’s Last Major Logistics Hub — Epicentr K reports the destruction of its last major logistics hub in Khmelnytskyi after ten attacks and multiple fires, following a severe week of attacks on the retailer's facilities across Ukraine, including locations in Chernihiv and Dnipro.

Russian Drone Strike Kills 6, Injures 13 in Lutsk as Zelensky Urges G7 to Force Moscow to Stop — Zelensky called on G7 leaders to force Russia to stop its attacks through sanctions and pressure after a Shahed strike killed six people and injured 13 in Lutsk on Wednesday, Oct. 14. In Rivne, a Russian drone wounded five people, including a child.

Peskov: Russia Did Not Break Trump’s ‘Energy Truce’ Because Terms Were Never Set — Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday ,Oct. 14 that US President Donald Trump’s energy truce was never defined, so Russia cannot be accused of breaking it. The latest strikes on Kyiv and Kharkiv’s power plants left at least 600,000 Ukrainian citizens without electricity, while the remarks deepened doubts over a deal announced on Sunday, Oct. 11, to which neither state formally agreed, although Ukrai

Russia to Sign Diesel Contracts With Washington Soon, Putin’s Money Man Says — Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of the Russian Direct Investment Fund, said on Wednesday that Moscow is signing contracts with Washington “in the next few days” to export Russian diesel. Media reports suggest the total volume – including those to the US and elsewhere – barely sustains half a day of US consumption.

Japan Summons Russian Ambassador to Protest Journalist’s Arrest — Russia’s FSB arrested a Japanese journalist while he was working on Sakhalin Island in the Far East, a territory disputed by Tokyo and Moscow. The journalist was flown to Moscow, with the Kremlin alleging he was suspected of espionage. Tokyo and media rights group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) have denied the allegations.

Two Veterans With Prosthetic Legs Conquer 6,476-Meter Himalayan Peak in Tribute to Ukraine’s Defenders — Two Ukrainian veterans who lost a leg in combat have summited Nepal’s 6,476-meter Mera Peak using prostheses. After more than a year of training, Havryliak and Greenwood dedicated the climb to Ukraine’s defenders and fallen soldiers.

Escaped Russian POW Reportedly Shoots 5 Ukrainian Troops Dead Near Kharkiv — A gunman killed five soldiers from Ukraine’s 72nd Mechanized Brigade in a residential house near Kharkiv on Oct. 13. The brigade said people believed to be Russian citizens may be involved, while investigators are considering several theories, including an escaped Russian captive and a Russian sabotage group. Officials have not confirmed any of these versions.

Zelensky Arrives in UK to Meet King Charles and Burnham — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Britain on Wednesday, Oct. 14, announcing an audience with King Charles III and security talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The visit comes as Britain pledges faster deliveries of air defense missiles to Ukraine.

‘Black Rus’ Sabotage Group Likely Responsible for Latvian Incursion — Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko denied his country’s involvement in the Oct. 6 incursions of the Latvian border, saying it was a false flag operation orchestrated by Riga. Shortly afterward, the little-known “Black Rus” sabotage group, thought to be a front for Russian or Belarusian intelligence services, claimed responsibility.

Kyiv Mayor Faces Questioning as Russian Attack Triggers Fresh Water Cuts — Kyiv authorities announced water disruptions once more in multiple districts following Russia’s overnight ballistic missile strikes, with the city’s CHP-4 power plant among the targets. Kyiv residents have named water disruptions a major concern this winter, while the mayor has been summoned for questioning amid longstanding animosity between Kyiv and local authorities.

Ukraine’s Lyman/Vivaldi Offensive Concludes With Solid Terrain Gains, Russian Losses — Ukraine’s 3rd Corps says Operation Vivaldi recaptured 277 km² and inflicted 8,000 Russian casualties near Lyman. 3rd Corps Commander Biletsky said coordinated infantry infiltrations and drone swarms disrupted Russian defenses and protected supply routes to Slovyansk and Kramatorsk.

‘We Are Watching You’: Poland Warns Musk Over Starlink — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski warned Elon Musk that European customers were watching his actions after Ukrainian officials reported new Starlink restrictions. Presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov said limits affecting terminals moving at high speed were introduced without warning and disrupted several military missions.

Ukraine’s Business Leaders to Tackle War Risks and Economic Resilience at 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum on Oct. 26 — The 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum will take place on Oct. 26, bringing together more than 500 business leaders, officials and investors. Discussions will focus on economic resilience, energy security, war-related risks and restoring growth as the World Bank forecasts 1.2% growth for Ukraine in 2026.

Canada’s Dominion Dynamics, Ukraine’s TENCORE Sign Deal to Build TerMIT Ground Vehicles in Canada — Ottawa-based Dominion Dynamics and Ukraine’s TENCORE signed a memorandum of understanding to manufacture the TerMIT unmanned ground vehicle in Canada and integrate Dominion’s AuraNet autonomy stack. The companies aim for production to start in 2027, with a TENCORE team leading technology transfers and the training of Canadian technicians. The deal follows a September Canada-Ukraine pledge to build

Allies Warn Ukraine of Delayed Missile Waves, Air Force Says — Ukraine received no allied warning before the first wave of Russia’s overnight ballistic missile attack, but partners provided alerts for three subsequent waves, Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said on Wednesday, Oct. 14. His clarification follows Zelensky’s complaints about missing warnings and assurances from Trump and Sybiha that US intelligence cooperation continues.

Trump’s Phantom Ceasefires Are a National Security Problem — Twice in one month President Trump announced falsely that he had negotiated a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. It is time to consider the implications. Congress must treat this as a matter of national security and demand an explanation.

Russian Overnight Strikes Target Kyiv CHP Plants and Kill Civilians Across Ukraine — Russian ballistic missiles targeted all 3 of Kyiv’s municipal CHP power plants and energy infrastructure in surrounding regions. Attacks across Ukraine also killed at least 5 civilians and injured dozens, damaging industrial facilities, railway infrastructure and residential buildings.

SpaceX Restricts Ukraine’s Military Starlink Without Warning, Disrupting Drone Missions, Defense Sources Say — Restrictions affecting military Starlink connectivity were detected overnight Ukrainian Defense Ministry sources told Kyiv Post. Officials are investigating the cause and checking preliminary indications that connections are interrupted for users moving at speeds above 160 kph (100mph).

US-Russia Diesel Deal: What’s The Big Idea? — Trump’s reported deal to import 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel and ease sanctions has sparked criticism across Europe. Commentators warn it could fund Russia’s war against Ukraine and weaken US credibility, while others say Europe must address its own reliance on Russian energy.

Moscow, Washington vs. Kyiv: Can Trump Force Ukraine to Capitulate? — US President Donald Trump’s recent statements are aligning with those coming from the Kremlin. What does this new Moscow-Washington alliance of convenience mean, and will these situational allies succeed in forcing Ukraine to capitulate to Russia?

Europe Must Switch Arms Production to ‘War Mode’ to Match Russia, Polish Defense Minister Says — Poland’s defense minister urged Europe to shift arms production into “war mode” to match Russia’s output of around 7 million munitions in 2025. Warsaw also criticized proposed EU budget cuts, arguing Europe must invest more in defense before it is too late.

‘Blatant Disrespect Toward America’: Zelensky Slams Russia’s Strike on Ukraine’s Energy Sector — Russia launched 39 missiles and 128 drones at Ukraine overnight, damaging 30 energy and oil and gas facilities. Zelensky urged Trump to impose stronger sanctions and provide more Patriot interceptors as at least 600,000 people lost electricity.

Nearly 500 Drones Head Toward Moscow as Russian Data Centers and Oil Facilities Face Attacks — Russian officials said nearly 500 drones headed toward Moscow overnight, disrupting airport operations. In Balakovo, residential buildings damaged, while OSINT analysts reported possible damage to industrial facilities and at least eight oil terminal tanks affected by a fire near Rostov-on-Don.

Russia Innovates for War, Not Prosperity — Putin inherited a country with scientific talent and industrial capacity. He has squandered that inheritance. Engineers are diverted toward weapons, and Russian is now beholden to China for much of its technological and industrial output.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 13, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 13, 2026.

Why Did Kadyrov Visit Azerbaijan? Analysts Point to Putin’s Interests and a Possible Escape Plan — Ramzan Kadyrov’s lavish reception in Azerbaijan has raised questions about the future of Putin’s Chechen ally. Analysts examine the Kremlin’s enduring ties with Baku, Kadyrov’s powerful security and business network, and allegations that he is seeking a safe haven for his family amid uncertainty over Russia’s political future.

Two Nights Without Missile Warnings – Zelensky Raises Alarm as Trump Denies Intelligence Cutoff — Ukraine received no advance allied warnings during Russian ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv on Oct. 12 and 13. Zelensky sounded the alarm without naming the country responsible. The failures followed an Axios report that US officials threatened to suspend intelligence sharing over Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. Trump denied any cutoff, while his new press secretary said she would look int

Shakhtar Dream of Champions League Return to Ukraine as London Keeps War in Spotlight — Shakhtar Donetsk will play their European home matches at Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge, with club chief executive Sergei Palkin saying the move will help keep Ukraine’s struggle in the international spotlight. The club has played in exile since 2014 and hopes one day to return to Ukraine.

UK to Fast-Track Air Defense Missiles for Ukraine as Burnham Hosts Zelensky in London — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street on Wednesday, Oct. 14, pledging accelerated deliveries of air defense missiles, additional military aid and tougher sanctions against Russia. London is also urging international partners to restrict Russian LNG exports and increase pressure on Moscow to halt attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv Power Plant, Killing 3, Injuring 26 – Zelensky Raises Alarm Over Missing Allied Warnings — Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s CHP-4 power plant and a nine-story apartment building late Tuesday, killing at least 3 people and injuring 26, including a child. Zelensky said Ukraine received no advance warning from Western partners for the second consecutive night.

12 Senators Sign Bipartisan Letter Urging Trump to Rescind Russian Diesel Deal — Twelve US senators – six Republicans and six Democrats – signed a joint
letter urging US President Donald Trump on Monday to rescind his Oct. 9 diesel arrangement with Russian President Vladimir Putin. They called it a betrayal of Ukraine and demanded the president to enforce the new Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, signed by Trump just three weeks before striking the deal with the Kremlin

Phantom Defense Buys Developer of KARAKURT Drone Net Launchers — Ukrainian counter-drone company Phantom Defense has acquired the full business and team behind KARAKURT net launchers, which military units have used in more than 50,000 kits over six months. It also introduced MANGAL, an AI-guided system with six net launchers and a one-second response time, built to protect vehicles, positions and unmanned ground vehicles.

Ireland Aims to Open All Remaining EU Accession Clusters for Ukraine by Year-End — The EU successfully opened Ukraine’s Clusters 2 and 3; the internal market, and competitiveness and inclusive growth on Tuesday, Oct. 13, a day after all 27 member states unanimously agreed to open them as Ukraine adopted a minority education law that Hungary had demanded in exchange for lifting its veto on the EU bid. Ireland’s minister of state for European affairs and defense said Ireland’s EU presidency aims t

Trump Denies US Has Stopped Sharing Intelligence With Ukraine — US President Donald Trump denied claims that Washington has stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine, following days of tensions between the US and Ukraine. The question arose after reports that the US threatened to cut intelligence and weapons purchases over Kyiv’s refinery strikes, and after Ukraine received no early warning of a Russian ballistic missile attack.

How Are Ukrainians Coping With Russia’s Attacks on Ukraine’s Energy Grid? — Ukrainians are already feeling the effects of Russia’s energy grid strikes ahead of winter. Blackouts can vary across the country, and with an energy truce uncertain, many Ukrainians interviewed by Kyiv Post raised concerns about water supplies and urged authorities to act now, learning lessons from 2025-26.

Russian Drone Strike on Rivne University Injures 30, Forces Students to Remote Learning — Russian forces struck a Rivne State Humanitarian University on Tuesday, Oct. 13, injuring 30 people, including university staff. The attack nearly burned out the music faculty’s premises, leaving its building unusable for in-person classes.

Russia’s Rassvet Satellites Could Give Drones Space-Based Control, Former HUR Official Warns — Russia launched about 32 Rassvet low-orbit satellites in 2026 as it works to build its own, domestic alternative to Starlink. Speaking to Interfax-Ukraine, former Deputy Head of the Defense Intelligence of Ukraine (HUR) Ilya Pavlenko warned that the network could give Russian drones real-time satellite control, deepen Moscow’s reliance on Chinese technology and further threaten Europe.

Russian Drone Attack Kills 1, Injures 2 in Pavlohrad — Russian forces launched a drone attack on Pavlohrad, killing one person and injuring two on Tuesday, Oct. 13. According to Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha, Russian drones and artillery struck four districts of the region nearly 40 times, injuring two people in the Nikopol area and causing fires in Dnipro earlier in the afternoon. The overall number of casualties in the region on Tuesday is one dea

Zelensky Says Kyiv Trails Even Frontline Regions on Resilience, Signals Changes in City Management — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday that Kyiv trails every other region, including frontline areas, in implementing its resilience plan. It was his second rebuke of Kyiv’s authorities in a week, and he said he is preparing decisions that include changing how the capital is managed, although no additional details were provided.

Ukrainian Startup Zvook Secures Investment From Czech DEPO Ventures — Czech venture capital firm DEPO Ventures made the first investment from its new Ukraine Fund into Zvook, a Ukrainian defense tech startup. This critical funding will support regional technological innovation and help scale the company's AI-powered acoustic threat-detection sensors.

Kyiv Calls WP’s 4-Point Peace Plan ‘American PR’ — Ukraine has pushed back against a Washington Post column describing an emerging “joint US-European peace proposal.” Presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn said its four components represented the views of some US officials expressed during talks in Florida, calling the report “good American PR.”

Ukraine Delays $2.3 Billion in Payments as Treasury Cash Runs Short — Ukraine has pushed about $876 million of spending to year-end, left $1.03 billion in payments unprocessed and suspended $404 million in VAT refunds, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko told the Verkhovna Rada. The Treasury is funding only defense, pensions, wages and social aid until the Single Treasury Account recovers.

US Intelligence Still Flows to Ukraine, Sybiha Says — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine continues receiving US intelligence, rejecting speculation that cooperation had been suspended. He said the delayed alert during Russia’s latest ballistic strike resulted from the type of weapon used against Ukraine.

Oil-Contaminated Birds Found On Shore By Drone-Hit Russian Tanker — Oil-soaked seabirds found dead and dying on Black Sea beaches dozens of km from the Aframax Rio tanker, struck and set ablaze by Ukrainian drones off Sochi on Oct 6. Russian claims of no structural damage or oil leak are contradicted by evidence of pollution and wildlife harm; Greenpeace warns of serious environmental impact.

Putin’s Protector in the White House — As Trump’s bromance with Putin gets warmer and fuzzier, Ukrainians and their supporters are astounded by how the leader of the most powerful democracy in the world has utterly abdicated the ideals Americans have always cherished and defended.

EBRD Expands Ukraine War-Risk Insurance to $168M — The EBRD is raising the capacity of its war-risk insurance facility to $168 million. Two new insurers are set to join the scheme and will also cover gas-related assets and goods in temporary storage.

Whitaker Says ‘No Change’ to Arms Flows to Kyiv via PURL — On Monday, US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker said that he knew of no change to Washington’s weapon policies to Ukraine via NATO, saying he does not wish to comment on “unconfirmed reports.” Whitaker also acknowledged Kyiv’s air defense shortage but said he viewed it as a “short-term challenge,” with “a lot of companies” working on alternatives to fill the gap.

Europe Pushes Back Against Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal, Vows to Keep Sanctions — European governments have criticized US President Donald Trump’s Russian diesel agreement and pledged to maintain pressure on Moscow. Their initial responses combine opposition to sanctions relief with calls to preserve US cooperation and secure a reciprocal halt to attacks on energy infrastructure.

France Boards Russian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Tanker Near Reunion Island — The French Navy intercepted and boarded the sanctioned oil tanker DF Peak more than 450 nautical miles south of Réunion. France suspects the vessel of using a false flag and participating in illegal fuel transportation linked to Russia’s shadow fleet.
CARTOON: When You’re Ready to do Anything for Your Partner... — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Zelensky Says Ukraine Received No Warning From Partners Before Russian Ballistic Missile Strike on Kyiv — Zelensky said Ukraine received no warning from its partners before Russia launched 5 ballistic missiles at civilian infrastructure in Kyiv. He said Russian attacks also killed four people and wounded 41 in Kharkiv, while 19 regions came under attack over two days despite a US-backed call for an energy ceasefire.

‘Not Right’: Finland Seeks EU Ban on Russian Tourist Visas — Finland is urging the EU to stop issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens until Moscow ends its war against Ukraine. Helsinki is also seeking restrictions targeting Vladimir Putin’s inner circle, Russian athletes linked to the state, and any former combatants.
British Defence Intelligence Update Ukraine 9 October , 2026 — Latest from the British Defence Intelligence.

Bulgaria to Summon Russian Ambassador After Attacks on Black Sea Ships — Bulgaria plans to summon Russia’s ambassador following attacks on commercial vessels near its territorial waters. All crew members aboard the Chelsea 3 survived and were rescued, while Ukraine said Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens were injured.

Russia Reportedly Strikes Dnipro With Guided Bombs, Wounding 64-Year-Old Man — Russian forces reportedly attacked Dnipro with guided aerial bombs on Oct. 13, injuring a 64-year-old man and damaging apartment buildings, vehicles, and transport infrastructure. The weapon type remains unconfirmed, and a previous suspected guided-bomb strike on the city was later identified as a Hrom-1 missile.

‘You’re Not Winning This Fight’: Kellogg Says Putin Shows Weakness as War Drags On — Former US envoy Kellogg said Ukraine should decide how to fight Russia, including whether to strike Russian refineries. He dismissed tensions between Trump and Zelensky as “noise” and urged continued pressure on Putin, arguing that Russia has failed to achieve its strategic goals.

The More Putin Escalates Attacks on Europe, the more Europe Should Support Ukraine — Europe’s best response to Russia’s escalating hybrid warfare is to strengthen support for Ukraine, which remains the Kremlin’s primary target. Germany has emerged as a key supporter, but growing political opposition and the cost of future aid threaten European unity.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 12, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 12, 2026.

Russia Launches Missile and Drone Attacks, Killing 2 in Kyiv and 4 in Kharkiv Despite Trump’s Ceasefire Claim — Russian missile and drone attacks killed two women in Kyiv and four people in Kharkiv overnight on Oct. 12-13. The strikes damaged residential buildings and civilian infrastructure across multiple regions, while attacks also killed a woman in Lozova.

IMF Warns Europe’s Growth Will Slow as Russia’s War, Middle East Crisis Drive Up Energy Costs — The International Monetary Fund forecasts eurozone growth of just 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, warning that Russia’s war against Ukraine and the Middle East conflict are driving up energy costs and prolonging inflation. At its World Economic Outlook briefing, IMF officials also warned of risks to Gulf economies and highlighted the growing dependence of global trade on artificial intelligence.

‘They Agreed Because I Said They Agreed’ – Trump Insists Ukraine, Russia Accepted Energy Ceasefire Despite Denials — US President Donald Trump insisted Monday, Oct. 12, that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire because he told them to, despite neither government confirming such a deal. Trump dismissed questions about continued Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and claimed Putin was more eager to reach a peace agreement than Zelensky. His remarks came amid growing

Merz Calls on Russia to Accept Energy Ceasefire Following Talks With Zelensky — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Russia to agree to an energy ceasefire following a phone conversation with President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday, Oct. 12. The leaders discussed renewed Russian attacks on civilian and energy facilities despite US President Donald Trump’s announcement of an energy truce.

‘No More Artificial Delays!’ – Lithuania Urges Faster Ukraine EU Accession — Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys urged the EU to accelerate Ukraine’s accession, calling membership a security guarantee for both Kyiv and Europe. His remarks followed Ukraine’s adoption of legislation protecting minority education rights, addressing a key Hungarian concern that had delayed accession negotiations.

Russian Missile Strike Destroys Kharkiv Apartment Entrance, Killing 4 and Injuring Dozens — Russian missile strikes killed 4 people and injured 41 in Kharkiv on Oct. 12, destroying an entrance section of a four-story apartment building. Rescuers pulled four people to safety, while a rescue worker was injured and search-and-rescue operations continued.
